added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed run's own gate arms. The reviewed manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite fields are both empty, so no same-command base arm is recorded. The run's head arms name no FAILED/ERROR id: two-files-committed.log (revision 0999bfe27) reports 7 passed EXIT=0, module-guard-final.log reports 4 passed EXIT=0, and pure-move-final.log reports EXIT=0 with an empty problems list. The one pre-repointing two-file arm (two-files-before.log, 5 failed at 590fe543d) records the failures the repoints fix, not failures the run added. I independently reran the three named gates at the reviewed head 0999bfe27 (pure-move EXIT=0 with 407 moved, guard 4 passed EXIT=0, two-file 7 passed EXIT=0): head minus base is empty, so added_failure_count 0 and added_failure_ids [].

findings.text: follow-on: after dispatch.py's removal from the allowlist the ratchet this test applies is the 50,000-estimated-token lane bound, not §3's stricter 40,000-token per-produced-module target, so a produced module growing past 40,000 (e.g. reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py, at 37,174 today) is not caught until it exceeds 50,000; §3's produced-module bound is measured in the landing fragment but no test fails when it is crossed.

follow-on: no clean whole-census gate exists at the reviewed head 0999bfe27. Every full census arm the run carries ended EXIT=2 — census-gate-complete.log (760 passed, 1 failed) at cb1d09bd5 and census-gate-final2.log (624 passed, 1 failed) at 590fe543d — and the manifest's tests line records only the two-file focused gate at the final head, so census cleanliness at 0999bfe27 rests on the coordinator's merged-head suite measure rather than the run's own log.
